temporary.rationale: BRD DOC-56CFA21523C1 section 6.2 / io Q2 ruling on ENC-PLN-082: expected_architecture.prod flips to arm64, and this class populates with the not-yet-migrated tranche, at the START of Phase 5 -- simultaneously, so CI never asserts a state the fleet contradicts. Phase 5 belongs to ENC-PLN-082, not this task (ENC-PLN-086 Wave 2, gamma-only, no production mutation). Production is 28/28 x86_64 today and Phase 5 has not started, so this class is correctly empty -- not because no exceptions are anticipated, but because the tranched migration that would populate it hasn't begun. See ENC-TSK-O82 worklog for the full reasoning.

permanent.rationale: SnapStart-retained functions per BRD section 4.4; arm64 SnapStart is Java-only. Seeded empty per ENC-TSK-O72's closed ruling: ENC-TSK-O70's census (28/28 in-scope production functions, cross-verified against a 231-function account-wide scan, corroborated by a 3-leg positive control) found 0 functions with SnapStart.ApplyOn != "None". Disposition counts: drop_and_flip=0, retain_and_hold=0, not_applicable=28 -- retain_and_hold's precondition (SnapStart currently enabled) is false for all 28, so the permanent class has no member to seed. This is a positive proof of emptiness, not an absence of evidence.
permanent._families_doc: ENC-TSK-P15 / ENC-ISS-669: the permanent class is not one exception, it is a CLASS of exceptions -- a function belongs here when the deviation from expected_architecture is a standing decision, not a migration-in-progress tranche (that's the temporary class, above). 'families' below names each standing decision individually, each with its own scoped rationale/terminal_state/ratchet, so a future addition to one family's reasoning can never be misread as also justifying the other's. The flat x86_64 list and the rationale/terminal_state/ratchet fields directly above are left untouched for backward compatibility with tools/verify_lambda_arch_parity.py's existing per-resource exceptions check (_validate_architecture_exceptions) and the ENC-TSK-O84 ratchet diff (_class_name_sets / diff_architecture_exceptions), both of which read this flat shape and must keep passing unmodified; 'families' is additive, read only by the newer cross-source reconciliation (AC-6, _validate_cross_source_reconciliation) and by humans.

snapstart_retained.description: Functions permanently retained on x86_64 because they depend on SnapStart, which is Java-only on arm64 (BRD section 4.4). Mirrors the flat x86_64 list above verbatim -- this is the same family, named, not a second one.
snapstart_retained.member_source: this file, architecture_exceptions.prod.permanent.x86_64 (the flat list above) -- authoritative, not duplicated data
snapstart_retained.rationale: See architecture_exceptions.prod.permanent.rationale above (ENC-TSK-O72 / ENC-TSK-O70 census). Restated here only so both permanent-class families are enumerable in one place.

devops_owned.description: ENC-ISS-669: Lambda functions owned and deployed by NX-2021-L/devops, a sibling repository that shares this AWS account and, for a subset of its functions, this repo's 'devops-' naming prefix. These functions have NEVER been in scope for enceladus's arm64 architecture contract or any enceladus deploy-validation check -- lambda_workflow_manifest.json's source_of_truth names ONE enceladus template (infrastructure/cloudformation/02-compute.yaml), and devops's Lambdas were never declared there because they are not enceladus's to declare. This is a CENSUS BOUNDARY ruling, not an architecture-migration exception: the arm64 contract does not extend to the whole AWS fleet, and this family says so explicitly rather than leaving the boundary implicit (which is exactly how ENC-ISS-669 went four functions deep before anyone noticed a fifth).
devops_owned.member_source: infrastructure/devops_lambda_ownership_snapshot.json#/functions[].function_name -- a pinned, hash-verified snapshot (see that file's own _doc and tools/verify_devops_ownership_snapshot.py), NOT a hand-copied list here. Membership is read from the snapshot at check time by tools/verify_lambda_arch_parity.py's _validate_cross_source_reconciliation (AC-6); this entry deliberately does not repeat the function names, so there is exactly one place they can drift out of sync with their provenance.
devops_owned.ownership_predicate: any live Lambda function whose FunctionName exactly matches a functions[].function_name entry in the pinned snapshot is owned by NX-2021-L/devops and resolves to NOT_APPLICABLE_ON_PLANE on every enceladus architecture-parity and deploy-validation check that would otherwise evaluate it. This is a name-match predicate against a governed, provenanced snapshot -- never a 'devops-' prefix heuristic, because dozens of enceladus's OWN functions (devops-changelog-api, devops-coordination-api, devops-graph-sync, ...) carry that same historical prefix from before the two repos split; a prefix match would misclassify them as devops-owned.
devops_owned.deploy_path_constraint: AC-7: the four functions.yaml-declared devops functions (devops-json-to-parquet-transformer, devops-glue-crawler-launcher, devops-adhoc-promotion, devops-platform-health) deploy exclusively through devops's 'Deploy Analytics Stack' workflow (GitHub Actions workflow id 245543976), which is disabled_manually under DVP-TSK-700. The fifth, devops-io-devops-mcp, deploys through its own separate, ACTIVE workflow (deploy-io-devops.yml) and is already arm64/python3.12. With workflow 245543976 disabled, the four functions.yaml functions have NO LIVE DEPLOY CHANNEL in either repo today -- 'just upgrade them to arm64' is not an available remediation, which is precisely why this is the permanent exception and not the temporary (migration-tranche) one. Re-enabling workflow 245543976 as a side effect of this task, or of any future arm64 migration work, is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE and PROHIBITED here -- that decision belongs to DVP-TSK-700 and whatever devops-side work eventually resolves it, not to an enceladus architecture-contract task.
devops_owned.rationale: io ruling: ENC-TSK-P15 (ENC-ISS-669). The organisational census-boundary ruling this family encodes: gamma-plane arm64 governance in this repo applies to functions this repo owns and declares; it was never meant to, and does not now, reach into a sibling repository's own estate. That boundary held for four functions by accident (nobody had occasion to invoke it) and broke for a fifth (devops-io-devops-mcp, declared nowhere in devops's own functions.yaml either) purely because no one had written the boundary down. This family is that boundary, written down.
devops_owned.terminal_state: permanent -- this is an organisational boundary (a different owning repository), not a migration state, so unlike the temporary class it does not shrink toward zero as work completes. It changes only if ownership itself changes (e.g. a function is formally transferred into this repo, at which point it leaves the snapshot and this family loses a member) or if devops's own estate grows (at which point the pinned snapshot gains a member via a reviewed pin-bump, per infrastructure/devops_lambda_ownership_snapshot.json's own refresh discipline).
devops_owned.ratchet: additions require BOTH an io ruling AND a corresponding reviewed edit to infrastructure/devops_lambda_ownership_snapshot.json (new pinned commit, new source digest(s), new functions[] entry with real provenance) -- a name cannot become exempt here by editing this manifest alone. Removals require the snapshot to stop naming the function (ownership transferred, or the function decommissioned).
